prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1347; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and stated that a wrist injury was sustained at the scene. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been informed of the claims process.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was inside the vehicle at the time of impact. The other driver's account matches the claimant's description of how the collision occurred.

Entry 3: Photographs of the vehicle show front-end damage consistent with the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy coverage period. The driver is named on the policy.

Entry 4: The reported wrist fracture is consistent with the type and force of a collision of this kind. Medical records show no prior injury to the same area of the body.

Entry 5: The claimant later provided additional minor details about the sequence of events, but the core account has remained the same across all statements. Witness statements and photographs continue to support the description.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course, with symptoms improving steadily and care tapering as recovery progressed. No further medical action is currently required, and the file will be reviewed upon receipt of the final treatment summary.
